title: Zero deviations and a model line at a medical-device contract manufacturer

organization.industry: Medical devices: single-use infusion sets and catheter assemblies built to OEM customer specifications
organization.size: About 430 employees; five assembly lines (Lines 1-5) on two shifts

presentingRequest: We have had zero quality deviations for nine straight months and record output. Line 3 is our best line by a wide margin and I want it to be the template for the plant. Please document what Line 3 does differently and help us roll it out to Lines 1, 2, 4 and 5, and tell us why those lines cannot match it. — Plant Manager, Kestrel Ridge Medical Assemblies

evidence.text: Since February we have logged zero deviations across all five lines, and Q3 2026 was our highest-output quarter ever at 2.31 million units. Line 3 has run at 118% of plan since June with no extra headcount and no overtime. The culture has changed: people own quality now instead of writing paperwork about it.

evidence.source: Quality management system: deviation / nonconformance report (NCR) log, Jan 2025 - Oct 2026
evidence.text: Jan 2025 - Jan 2026: 182 deviation reports, average 14.0 per month (range 9-21), raised on all five lines. February 2026: 3 reports. March - October 2026: 0 reports on any line. No deviation has been raised by any line since 2026-02-17.

evidence.source: HR policy memo 'Line Supervisor Quality Incentive', dated 2026-01-19, signed by the Plant Manager and the HR Director
evidence.text: Effective 1 February 2026, each deviation report attributed to a line deducts 4% of that line supervisor's quarterly bonus, up to a maximum deduction of 40%. Lot rejections recorded by the independent QC lab at final inspection are a Regulatory function and are not attributed to line supervisors under this incentive. Stated purpose: 'to drive ownership of first-time quality'.

evidence.source: Production reports by line (MES), Jan - Oct 2026
evidence.text: Plan attainment Jan-May vs Jun-Oct 2026: Line 1 100% -> 95%; Line 2 98% -> 98%; Line 3 101% -> 118%; Line 4 99% -> 91%; Line 5 97% -> 97%. Line 3 rostered headcount is 22 technicians in both periods; overtime booked to Line 3 is zero in both periods. Plant units Feb-Oct 2026 are 9% above Feb-Oct 2025. Line 3 produced 34% of plant units Apr-Oct 2026.

We run tight: 5S, a ten-minute huddle at every shift start, and everyone knows the targets. We have done the huddles since early 2025. We don't need to write deviations any more because we catch problems early and deal with them at the station. I run the line with my 22 people.
The drop in deviations is the payoff from our new first-pass quality training program. We invested heavily in it and the results speak for themselves.

evidence.source: Learning management system: training and certification records
evidence.text: The first-pass quality training program launched on 2026-03-09. Completion across all technicians: 40% by 30 June, 78% by 31 October; Line 3 completion was 45% by 30 June. Bonding-station certification register: of the 7 technicians from other lines most frequently badged into the Line 3 cell since June (see E13), 5 hold no Line 3 luer-bonding certification.

evidence.source: Ethics hotline report #2026-031, received 2026-08-27 (anonymous; reporter declined follow-up contact)
evidence.text: Since the bonus change, on Line 3 leaking or mis-bonded subassemblies are pulled on second shift and re-bonded in the back cage with new connectors and adhesive. No NCR tag is put on them and the rework is not written in the device history record. People from other lines are brought in to keep the numbers up. Everyone knows that whoever writes it up costs the supervisor money.

evidence.source: Corporate ethics committee case log, case #2026-031
evidence.text: 2026-09-03: case forwarded to the Plant Manager for local resolution. 2026-09-20: closed, 'no evidence found'. Closure note lists one action: the Plant Manager discussed the allegation with the Line 3 Supervisor, who denied it. No records review, no walk-through of the back cage and no other interviews are recorded.

evidence.source: Purchasing records and buyer notes, Feb - Oct 2026 vs Feb - Oct 2025
evidence.text: Purchases of replacement components and scrap-allowance material (tubing, luer connectors, bonding adhesive) are up 30% on the prior-year period while plant output is up 9%. The increase starts in February 2026. These purchases are booked to a single plant-level cost centre and are not attributed by line. Buyer note: all five lines switched to a lower-cost tubing supplier on 2026-04-14; incoming-inspection rejection rate for the new supplier's tubing is 1.1% vs 1.0% for the previous supplier.

evidence.source: Complaint reports from two OEM customers (Halvorsen Medical, Brightwater Infusion), compiled by Customer Quality
evidence.text: Complaint rate per million units shipped: 2025 average 11 ppm; Q1 2026 12 ppm; Q2 2026 19 ppm; Q3 2026 31 ppm. Of 58 complaints received Apr-Oct 2026 with a traceable lot code, 46 are leaks at the luer bond joint and 41 (71%) trace to Line 3 lots; Lines 2 and 5 together (31% of units, same tubing as all other lines) account for 6. Median lag from manufacture to complaint receipt is 9 weeks, so most Q2 complaints concern units built in February-March 2026.

evidence.source: Independent QC laboratory (reports to Regulatory Affairs, not to the plant): final-inspection AQL lot rejection data
evidence.text: Lot rejection rate at final inspection: 2025 average 0.8%; Feb-Oct 2026 average 1.3%. The increase appears on lots from all five lines; Line 3 lots rose from 1.1% to 1.9%. Leading rejection cause in 2026 is luer bond integrity.

evidence.source: Operations analyst reconciliation of badge-access data against timesheets, Jan - Oct 2026
evidence.text: From the first week of June, between 4 and 7 technicians whose home lines are Line 1 or Line 4 badge into the Line 3 cell on most working days (average 5.3 per day), while their timesheets charge all hours to their home lines. No such pattern exists Jan-May. Including these badge hours, Line 3 output per technician-hour is 41.2 units Jun-Oct vs 40.8 Jan-May and 41.0 for 2025.
Since about June I'm told to lend people whenever Line 3 asks. It's not on paper and my line takes the hit on attainment. I'd rather not say who tells me. I'm not going to make a fuss about it.

evidence.source: Technician interviews, 8 technicians from Lines 1, 3 and 4 (conducted by the engagement team, 2026-11-06 to 2026-11-07)
evidence.text: Six of eight declined to discuss quality topics. Two said that people who wrote NCRs last year were moved to night shift. One Line 3 technician said: 'You just fix it and move on now. Nobody writes anything.' None would confirm or deny the back-cage rework.

evidence.source: Anonymous plant pulse survey, September 2026 (n = 311, response rate 74%)
evidence.text: Agreement with 'I can raise a quality concern without fear of negative consequences' fell from 71% (September 2025) to 38%. Agreement with 'My supervisor wants to hear about defects' fell from 68% to 34%. Declines are similar on all five lines.

evidence.source: Internal audit report IA-2025-14 on manufacturing quality, issued 2025-11-21
evidence.text: In 2025 Line 3 generated 38% of all plant deviations, most of them luer bond leaks traced to cure-time variability at the bonding station. Corrective action CAPA-2025-117 was opened. As of 2026-10-31 the CAPA remains open and the change-control log records no process or equipment change to any bonding station since the audit.

hypotheses.text: Product quality has genuinely improved plant-wide in 2026; the zero deviation count reflects a real reduction in nonconformances.
Nonconformances are still occurring on all lines but are no longer being reported; deviation reporting has been suppressed.
Line 3's output advantage since June comes from superior, transferable working practices (5S, shift huddles, team ownership).
The April switch to a lower-cost tubing supplier is the main cause of the rise in customer complaints.
The first-pass quality training program is what drove deviations down to zero.
The Plant Manager knows about and is directing the off-the-books lending of technicians to Line 3.

edges.from: Supervisor bonus penalty per deviation report (effective 2026-02-01)
edges.to: Fall of deviation reports to zero

edges.from: Off-the-books borrowing of technicians from Lines 1 and 4
edges.to: Line 3 record output (118% of plan since June)
30% increase in replacement-component and scrap-allowance purchases
Rise in customer luer-bond leak complaints

edges.from: Switch to the lower-cost tubing supplier (2026-04-14)

actions.text: Adopt Line 3 as the plant model: roll out its practices to all lines and raise every line's output target to Line 3's current attainment level.

Suspend the deviation-count penalty in supervisor bonuses now, issue a written non-retaliation commitment, and announce a time-limited amnesty for reporting previously unrecorded nonconformances and rework.

Commission an investigation led from outside the plant's reporting line (Regulatory Affairs / corporate quality) that reconciles Line 3 device history records, rework-area material use, badge and timesheet data and complaint lot traceability, and assesses risk for lots already shipped, with protection for the hotline reporter.
Discipline the Line 3 Supervisor now for falsified records and off-the-books labor.
Ask the Plant Manager to identify the hotline reporter so the allegation can be followed up directly with them.

evidenceRequests.text: Line 3 device history records and rework-area adhesive/component issue logs, reconciled against lot output, Feb-Oct 2026
Complained-unit lots cross-referenced with the badge IDs and certifications of technicians who built each lot
Messages and approvals showing who requested or authorized technician lending to Line 3
Component kitting / material issue records by line (to attribute the purchase increase)
Industry benchmark of output per line for comparable contract manufacturers
Plant employee engagement survey results for 2023 and 2024
